chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the traveler who performs salat (prayer) behind the resident. He said: He performs two rak'ahs and then goes wherever he wishes.

key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler, meaning the person under the legal ruling of travel
key_terms.الْمُقِيمِ: the resident, meaning one who is not traveling and prays the full salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَيْثُ شَاءَ: wherever he wishes, indicating freedom to leave after completing his own obligation
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind, meaning in congregational following of another worshipper or Imam
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rak'ahs, referring to the shortened salat (prayer) of the traveler

ai.seo_question: How does a traveler perform salat (prayer) behind a resident according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a traveler praying behind a resident Imam. It states that the traveler performs two rak'ahs, in accordance with the ruling of shortened salat (prayer) during travel, and may then depart as he wishes.
